bugs.what: Internal room/scene IDs occasionally leak into player-facing travel text instead of the proper place name, e.g. 'You travel to ir_miners_hall.', 'You travel to fd_net_hall.', 'You travel to wm_moor_2_2.', 'You travel to wm_record_house.'

At a location with a paginated menu ('more in this room'), acting on a stale remembered menu number from before paging can silently land on the wrong page and produce 'No action N' instead of executing the intended choice, forcing a manual look/repage to recover.

A companion quest (Two Keepers, One Covenant) can trigger asking the player to carry a question to an NPC (Keeper Rowan) already fully talked-to and left behind hours of play earlier, with no way to complete it short of a very long backtrack — and no warning that crossing the Pass Gate into Marrowgate permanently forfeits it.

confusions: Wardmoor's open moor (Cairn Field/Twin Ruts/Sedge Flat/Hut Path/Peat Score, etc.) has many visually similar tiles and 'get your bearings' never actually named the two active side-quest destinations (Boot-Track Hollow for the Lost Sentry, the beacon hill for the Dark Beacon) after the first mention, so both were abandoned unfound despite real effort.

The game doesn't warn before the Pass Gate that any companion-hold grief left unresolved becomes permanently unresolved once you cross toward Marrowgate — this is stated once in passing dialogue but easy to miss and irreversible.
suggestions: Strip internal scene-id strings from the 'You travel to X' text everywhere, not just most places.
Persist the current menu page reliably so an action number typed right after a 'more' expansion never resolves against the wrong page.
Have 'get your bearings' surface named quest-destination hints (not just static landmarks) so distant sub-quests like the Lost Sentry/Dark Beacon stay findable without exhaustive grid-walking.
Surface a one-time explicit confirmation ('crossing here leaves N holds/quests behind for good — continue?') at the Pass Gate, since it's a hard point of no return for a lot of accumulated content.
